Key Findings & Recommendations (full 4-year dataset)

  • Discount ceiling varies by category: Furniture turns unprofitable above ~21-30% discount; Technology holds up to ~31-40%. A single company-wide discount cap doesn't fit the data — set it per category.
  • Tables, Bookcases and Supplies are structural losses ($-17.7k, $-3.5k, $-1.2k respectively) — not a clearance or demand problem, since order volume for these grew every year. Their pre-set discount tier is simply too deep for their margin structure.
  • Machines quietly underperforms: $189k in sales but only 1.8% margin — high volume, near break-even, easy to overlook next to outright losses.
  • Texas is the single biggest dollar loss (-$25.7k on $170k sales); Ohio has the worst percentage margin (-21.7%). Five states (TX, OH, IL, PA, NC) are net-negative despite real sales volume.
  • Best combination to grow: Office Supplies × Home Office (21% margin) and Technology × Corporate (18%) — Furniture is weak across every segment (2-3%).
These findings reference the full dataset; the charts above respond to the filters.
